oracle_clues: The change passes `descr->has_nan_na` into `string_to_pyfloat(...)` / `string_to_pycomplex(...)` instead of calling them without that argument, in `numpy/_core/src/multiarray/stringdtype/casts.cpp`.
A comment states: coercing one component of a complex to the NaN-like missing-data sentinel is lossy, so call sites raise a `ComplexWarning`.

The NaN-like missing-data sentinel path assigns the destination `out` value to `(npy_longdouble)NPY_NAN` and continues (skips normal parsing) when `is_nan_na` is set by `load_numeric_string(..., &is_nan_na, ...)`.
Complex values are considered NaN-like if either the real or imaginary component is NaN (mirroring `np.isnan` behavior for complex).

category_specific_evidence: NaN-like missing-data sentinel handling: if `is_nan_na` is set by `load_numeric_string(..., &is_nan_na, ...)`, the destination `out` value is assigned `(npy_longdouble)NPY_NAN` and the loop continues (skipping normal parsing).

Special values involved: NaN (including NaN-like sentinel). For complex values, “Complex values follow np.isnan (either component NaN)”—i.e., complex is considered NaN-like if either the real component or the imaginary component is NaN.
Complex coercion is lossy: call sites raise a `ComplexWarning` when complex values are coerced to the NaN-like missing-data sentinel.

Dtype-specific NaN detection logic is explicit: `npy_half` uses `npy_half_isnan`, complex float/double/longdouble use `npy_isnan` on `npy_creal/npy_cimag` (or float variants), and other real types use `npy_isnan(val)`.
No evidence is provided for handling of +/-inf, signed zero, or subnormals in this passage.
reproduction_risks: Assuming other special values (±inf, signed zero, subnormals) are part of the NaN-like sentinel behavior—passages only explicitly describe NaN and complex-NaN (either component NaN).
Not accounting for complex-specific behavior: NaN detection for complex uses `np.isnan` on either component, and coercing such values to the sentinel is lossy and can trigger `ComplexWarning`.
